# Objective

On a 4K display at 300% scaling, hint labels render ~1/3 of their intended
physical size (barely readable). Make label sizes DPI-correct while leaving
cursor targeting untouched.

# Root cause

The overlay window is sized `Bounds / scale` DIP and `layoutGrid` gets a
`ScaleTransform(1/scale)` (`Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs:57`) to map the
physical-pixel hint coordinates into that DIP window. That transform cancels
WPF's `×scale` DPI render for **sizes**: text drawn at `_fontSize` (e.g. 14,
`Views/HintCanvas.cs:193,198`) ends up at `14 × (1/scale) × scale = 14 physical
px` regardless of DPI. On a 4K panel 14 physical px is ~1.5 mm — tiny. `Pad`
(`:41`) and the corner radius (`:236`) are frozen the same way. Positions are
correct (physical → DIP → physical round-trips), which is why labels land in the
right place but at the wrong size.

# Approach (scale size constants by `scale`, leave positions in physical px)

Option A — minimal, targeting-safe:

- Add a `DpiScale` property to `HintCanvas` (default 1.0). Setter rebuilds
  `FormattedText` and re-renders all hints (emSize depends on it).
- In `BuildFormatted`, use `_fontSize * DpiScale` for the `FormattedText` emSize.
- In `RenderHint`, scale `Pad` and the corner radius by `DpiScale`.
- Name the canvas in `OverlayView.xaml` (`x:Name="hintCanvas"`) and set
  `hintCanvas.DpiScale = _scaleX` in `OnLoaded` (right after the existing
  `TransformToDevice` read).

Net: text → `(fontSize·s) × (1/s) × s = fontSize·s` physical px = DPI-correct
(same physical size as `fontSize` at 100%). The existing `HintFontSize` knob
becomes meaningful again on high-DPI.

Rejected Option B (drop the `1/scale` transform, divide display coords by scale,
draw at native DIP): touches the `PointHint` model and the cursor-targeting
math, which `mouse_event` relies on — too risky for the size-only symptom.

# Files

- `src/HuntAndPeck/Views/HintCanvas.cs` — `DpiScale` property + scaled emSize /
  pad / radius.
- `src/HuntAndPeck/Views/OverlayView.xaml` — `x:Name="hintCanvas"`.
- `src/HuntAndPeck/Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs` — set `hintCanvas.DpiScale`.

No `.csproj`, no `App.config`, no model change. `FormattedText` keeps the 6-arg
ctor (the `pixelsPerDip` overload needs .NET 4.7+; we target 4.5.1).

# Risks / non-goals

- **Cannot self-test on Linux** (WPF render) — CI compile + manual test on the
  4K / 300% Windows box.
- **Mixed-DPI multi-monitor** (e.g. 4K@300% + 1080p@100%): scale is captured once
  at load (same as the existing `LayoutTransform`), so labels would be wrong-
  sized on a second monitor at a *different* DPI. Pre-existing limitation; not
  addressed here (YAGNI — reported bug is single-monitor 4K).
- One extra `BuildFormatted` at overlay-open if `HintsSource` binds before
  `DpiScale` is set; negligible vs. the existing O(N) build.
- `DebugOverlayView` left alone (different render path; debug surface).

# Verification

- CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`, `windows-latest`) compiles + xUnit green.
- Manual on the 4K / 300% box: labels render at a readable physical size (≈ the
  same physical size as on a 1080p@100% display); positions still land on the
  correct click targets; `HintFontSize` still tunes the size.
